questions.stem:
Aspartame, an artificial sweetener, is a dipeptide aspartyl phenylalanine methyl ester. The structure of aspartame is
(Structures of phenylalanine and aspartic acid are given below.)
questions.solution: “Aspartyl phenylalanine methyl ester” means the α-COOH of aspartic acid forms the peptide bond with the NH₂ of phenylalanine, and phenylalanine’s COOH is the methyl ester; aspartic acid keeps its free α-NH₂ and its side-chain CH₂COOH. Option (B) shows exactly this, with both residues in the L configuration as in the given structures. (A) links through the side-chain (β) carboxyl of aspartic acid, (C) is a Phe–Asp dipeptide, and (D) puts the methyl ester on aspartic acid’s side chain and leaves phenylalanine as a free acid.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
Reaction of iso-propylbenzene with O₂ followed by the treatment with H₃O⁺ forms phenol and a by-product P. Reaction of P with 3 equivalents of Cl₂ gives compound Q. Treatment of Q with Ca(OH)₂ produces compound R and calcium salt S.
The correct statement(s) regarding P, Q, R and S is(are)

options.text: Reaction of P with R in the presence of KOH followed by acidification gives the compound shown
Reaction of R with O₂ in the presence of light gives phosgene gas
Q reacts with aqueous NaOH to produce Cl₃CCH₂OH and Cl₃CCOONa

questions.solution: The cumene process gives phenol and acetone (P). Three Cl₂ chlorinate one methyl group to give 1,1,1-trichloroacetone (Q), which Ca(OH)₂ cleaves in the haloform reaction to chloroform (R) and calcium acetate (S). (A) Base deprotonates CHCl₃ and CCl₃⁻ adds to acetone, giving chloretone, (CH₃)₂C(OH)CCl₃ — true. (B) Chloroform is oxidised by air in light to phosgene, COCl₂ — true. (C) Aqueous NaOH again effects the haloform cleavage of Q, giving CHCl₃ and CH₃COONa, not Cl₃CCH₂OH and Cl₃CCOONa — false. (D) Dry distillation of calcium acetate gives acetone — true.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
Complete reaction of acetaldehyde with excess formaldehyde, upon heating with conc. NaOH solution, gives P and Q. Compound P does not give Tollens’ test, whereas Q on acidification gives positive Tollens’ test. Treatment of P with excess cyclohexanone in the presence of catalytic amount of p-toluenesulfonic acid (PTSA) gives product R.
Sum of the number of methylene groups (-CH₂-) and oxygen atoms in R is ______.
questions.solution: Three crossed aldol additions of HCHO to the α-carbon of acetaldehyde give (HOCH₂)₃C–CHO, and a crossed Cannizzaro reaction with more HCHO reduces it to pentaerythritol C(CH₂OH)₄ (P) while HCHO becomes formate (Q; formic acid gives Tollens’ test). With excess cyclohexanone and PTSA, each pair of CH₂OH groups forms a 1,3-dioxane ketal, giving a dispiro bis-ketal R. CH₂ count: 4 from pentaerythritol + 5 in each cyclohexane ring × 2 = 14; oxygen atoms = 4. Sum = 18.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
In the following reaction sequence, the major product P is formed.
HC≡C–(CH₂)₁₅–CO₂Et —i) Hg²⁺, H₃O⁺ ii) Zn-Hg/HCl iii) H₃O⁺, Δ→ P
Glycerol reacts completely with excess P in the presence of an acid catalyst to form Q. Reaction of Q with excess NaOH followed by the treatment with CaCl₂ yields Ca-soap R, quantitatively.
Starting with one mole of Q, the amount of R produced in gram is ______.
[Given, atomic weight: H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, Na = 23, Cl = 35, Ca = 40]
questions.solution: Hg²⁺-catalysed hydration of the terminal alkyne gives the methyl ketone CH₃CO(CH₂)₁₅CO₂Et; Clemmensen reduction turns C=O into CH₂, and acid hydrolysis of the ester gives stearic acid, CH₃(CH₂)₁₆COOH (P). Glycerol + 3 P → tristearin (Q). Saponification gives 3 mol sodium stearate per mole of Q, and CaCl₂ precipitates calcium stearate (C₁₇H₃₅COO)₂Ca, M = 606. Three stearate ions give 1.5 mol of R: 1.5 × 606 = 909 g.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
List-I contains various reaction sequences and List-II contains the possible products. Match each entry in List-I with the appropriate entry in List-II and choose the correct option.
List-I
(P) Cyclohexene —i) O₃, Zn ii) aq. NaOH, Δ iii) ethylene glycol, PTSA iv) a) BH₃, b) H₂O₂, NaOH v) H₃O⁺ vi) NaBH₄→
(Q) 1-Methylcyclohexene —i) O₃, Zn ii) aq. NaOH, Δ iii) ethylene glycol, PTSA iv) a) BH₃, b) H₂O₂, NaOH v) H₃O⁺ vi) NaBH₄→
(R) 2-Methylcyclopent-2-en-1-one —i) ethylene glycol, PTSA ii) a) Hg(OAc)₂, H₂O, b) NaBH₄ iii) H₃O⁺ iv) NaBH₄→
(S) 2-Methylcyclopent-2-en-1-one —i) ethylene glycol, PTSA ii) a) BH₃, b) H₂O₂, NaOH iii) H₃O⁺ iv) NaBH₄→
List-II: (1)–(5) structures shown
questions.solution: (P) Ozonolysis gives hexanedial; intramolecular aldol condensation gives cyclopent-1-enecarbaldehyde. After protecting CHO as an acetal, hydroboration puts OH on the ring carbon away from the substituent; deprotection and NaBH₄ give 2-(hydroxymethyl)cyclopentanol (3). (Q) Ozonolysis gives 6-oxoheptanal; the ketone’s CH₂ enolate attacks the more electrophilic aldehyde, giving 1-acetylcyclopentene, and the same sequence gives 1-(2-hydroxycyclopentyl)ethanol (5). (R) After ketal protection, oxymercuration–demercuration adds OH (Markovnikov) to the methyl-bearing carbon; deprotection and NaBH₄ give 1-methylcyclopentane-1,2-diol (4). (S) Hydroboration instead puts OH on the CH carbon (anti-Markovnikov), giving 2-methylcyclopentane-1,3-diol (1). So P-3, Q-5, R-4, S-1.

questions.stem:
List-I contains various reaction sequences and List-II contains different phenolic compounds. Match each entry in List-I with the appropriate entry in List-II and choose the correct option.
List-I
(P) Benzenesulfonic acid —i) molten NaOH, H₃O⁺ ii) Conc. HNO₃→
(Q) Nitrobenzene —i) Conc. HNO₃ / Conc. H₂SO₄ ii) Sn / HCl iii) NaNO₂ /HCl, 0 - 5 °C, iv) H₂O v) Conc. HNO₃ / Conc. H₂SO₄→
(R) Resorcinol —i) Conc. H₂SO₄ ii) Conc. HNO₃ iii) H₃O⁺, Δ→
(S) Toluene —i) a) KMnO₄ / KOH, Δ; b) H₃O⁺ ii) Conc. HNO₃ / Conc. H₂SO₄, Δ iii) a) SOCl₂, b) NH₃ iv) Br₂, NaOH v) NaNO₂ / HCl, 0 - 5 °C vi) H₂O→
List-II: (1)–(5) structures shown
questions.solution: (P) Alkali fusion gives phenol, and concentrated HNO₃ nitrates it fully to picric acid, 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (3). (Q) Nitration gives m-dinitrobenzene; Sn/HCl gives m-phenylenediamine, bis-diazotisation and hydrolysis give resorcinol, and nitration gives 2,4,6-trinitroresorcinol (5). (R) Sulfonation blocks the 4- and 6-positions of resorcinol, nitration then occurs at C-2, and steam/acid removes the SO₃H groups, giving 2-nitroresorcinol (4). (S) Toluene → benzoic acid; hot mixed acid gives 3,5-dinitrobenzoic acid (COOH is meta-directing) → amide → Hofmann degradation to 3,5-dinitroaniline → diazotisation/hydrolysis to 3,5-dinitrophenol (1). So P-3, Q-5, R-4, S-1.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper
